meta.title: Nasser, AI engineer and software engineer | cod by nasser
meta.description: I’m Nasser, AI engineer and software engineer. I adapted large language models in a project with Sberbank and built a Telegram platform with real users.

hero.title: I’m Nasser.
hero.say: I build smart systems with my own hands, and run them myself after launch.

manifesto.quote: “Alas for those that never sing, but die with all their music in them!”
manifesto.question: What is the richest land in the world?
guesses: One said: the oil lands of the Gulf.
Another said: the diamond mines of Africa.
manifesto.why: That is where millions went, carrying great ideas, dreams and talents that never saw the light of day. No one ever benefited from them.
manifesto.source: The story comes from Todd Henry’s book “Die Empty”.
manifesto.title: Don’t bury your idea with you.
lines: Don’t put it off until it’s too late. Bring out your best, and leave a mark worth remembering.
Every idea starts as a ghost only its owner can see. Put it off, and it ends up there too.
Code is what catches it and makes it work.
Tell me in your own words. I turn them into a system that works, and I stay with it after launch.
manifesto.name: That’s why the name is one letter short: cod isn’t complete without your idea.

story.title: How I work
story.lead: I build smart systems that understand your work, not generic tools that understand everything except your business.

points.title: My field
points.text: Artificial intelligence: machine learning and deep learning, and customising large language models so they work on their owner’s data.

points.title: I stay after launch
points.text: I don’t hand over a system and walk away. I run it myself with people who actually use it, and improve it based on what I see.

points.title: For business owners
points.text: I put all of this at their service: from managing social media accounts and creating content to systems that work for them.

skills.title: Technical skills
skills.intro: The tools I work with, grouped by field.

idea.title: Your idea, from the first word to a working system.
idea.intro: You don’t need to know the solution. You only need to know what’s giving you trouble, and I’ll walk the rest with you, one step at a time.

steps.title: I listen
steps.text: You tell me your idea or problem in your own words. No technical terms needed.

steps.title: I write it down
steps.text: I write the idea down and keep it exactly as you said it, so nothing gets lost.

steps.title: I ask
steps.text: The hard questions before any line of code: who is this for? Why now? And what happens if it isn’t built?

steps.title: I study
steps.text: A simple feasibility check and a look at the market and competitors, so you know where the value is, and where the profit is.

steps.title: I build the core
steps.text: I start with the part that actually solves the problem, before any extras.

steps.title: I measure and improve
steps.text: Numbers that show whether it works, and improvement that continues after delivery.

faq.title: Before you request
faq.intro: What people ask most before any project starts.

items.q: How much will my project cost?
items.a: The price is set once I understand your project, and I send it to you in writing, with what it includes and what it doesn’t. Projects have a fixed price for each stage; running and managing them is a monthly subscription.
It depends on the size of the work. The timeline is written in the offer before we start, and at every stage you know what’s done and what’s left.

items.q: Who owns the system after delivery?
items.a: That is written in the agreement before we start: what you own, who runs it, and what running it costs, if anything.

items.q: Do you work with projects outside Iraq?
items.a: Yes, remotely, in Arabic, English and Russian.
I stay with you: I run what I built if you want, maintain it and develop it, so you’re never left alone with a tool you don’t understand.
I only ask for the data the work needs, and before you send it we agree on who sees it and where it’s kept.

items.q: Do you guarantee a number of followers or sales?
items.a: No. I guarantee the work, the plan and an honest report. I build a real audience that cares about your work, and I don’t buy followers.
Write what’s troubling you in one message from the request page, or on WhatsApp. I read it myself, and reply.
